issues.t: Transmission lights flash and car goes into limp mode
issues.sym: The transmission warning lights on the dash flash, the car may hold one gear (often third or fourth), and it can feel sluggish. Some cars also refuse to start until the shifter is moved.
issues.why: The park/neutral position switch on the side of the AW30-40 automatic sits near the hot exhaust and its contacts get dirty or burnt. A bad gear position signal makes the transmission computer fall back to a safe mode. Corroded connectors on the transmission can do the same.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read. If the switch is the cause, a quality original-type switch fixes it. Avoid long drives while it is stuck in one gear, because the fluid can overheat.

issues.t: Transmission overheats and wears out early
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, rough or busy shifting, a burnt smell from the fluid, or the transmission lights coming on after a hard climb or towing.
issues.why: The AW30-40 in these cars runs hot when pulling hard at low engine speed, and Volvo called the fluid lifetime, so many were never changed. Heat breaks the fluid down and wears the clutches.
issues.next: Check the fluid level hot and its smell. A fluid flush done in stages often smooths early symptoms; an extra cooler helps if you tow or live somewhere hot. Slipping that a flush does not cure usually means a rebuild.

issues.t: Shudder when the torque converter locks up
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration, like driving over rumble strips, at light throttle in slow traffic or around 40-50 mph.
issues.why: The lock-up solenoid in the transmission can stick, so the torque converter clutch grabs and releases unevenly. Old fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Start with a fluid flush. If the shudder stays, have the lock-up solenoid replaced.

issues.t: Timing belt or tensioner failure
issues.sym: A squeal or rattle from the front of the engine, then the engine suddenly quits and cranks but will not start.
issues.why: This 2.9L six is an interference engine. If the timing belt, its tensioner or an idler pulley fails, the valves hit the pistons. Tensioner and pulley failures have been reported before 100,000 miles.
issues.next: If the belt history is unknown, replace the belt, tensioner and idler pulleys together now. If the belt has already broken, do not keep cranking the engine; have a shop check for bent valves.

issues.t: Loss of oil pressure from broken oil pump part
issues.sym: The oil pressure light comes on or flickers, and the engine may start ticking or knocking.
issues.why: Some late-1998 engines got an oil pump with a plastic pressure relief piston that can break apart, so the pump stops building pressure.
issues.next: Stop the engine right away if the oil light stays on. Have the oil pressure tested with a gauge; the fix is an oil pump with the later metal relief piston.

issues.t: Fuel leak from fuel rail plug
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell in the engine bay or wet fuel on top of the engine.
issues.why: The fuel rail used on 960-family engines up to 1997 has a factory plug that can start to seep fuel. Volvo changed the rail design from 1998.
issues.next: A fuel leak near a hot engine is a fire risk. Stop driving and have the fuel rail inspected and replaced if it is wet.

issues.t: Hard starting from sticking exhaust valves
issues.sym: Hard starting or no-start, especially after short trips in cold weather, with rough running and fouled spark plugs.
issues.why: Carbon deposits build up on the exhaust valve stems and stop the valves from closing fully. Lots of short, cold trips make it worse.
issues.next: Volvo advised switching to synthetic oil and taking regular longer drives at higher engine speed. If it keeps happening, a compression test shows whether the cylinder head needs work.

issues.t: Engine oil leaks from seals and oil cooler
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell, or oil wetting the back of the engine.
issues.why: Common leak points on this engine are the rear main seal, the rear camshaft seals, the oil cooler O-rings and the valve cover. A clogged crankcase breather (flame trap) raises pressure inside the engine and pushes oil past seals.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Clean or replace the breather first, since it is simple and can stop new leaks. Seal and O-ring repairs can follow based on how bad the leak is.

issues.t: Idle surge or no-start from coolant temperature sensor
issues.sym: The engine idles high (2,500-3,000 rpm) or surges, is hard to start when hot, or will not start, sometimes with the check engine light on.
issues.why: A failing engine coolant temperature sensor sends the wrong temperature to the engine computer, so it adds the wrong amount of fuel.
issues.next: Have the sensor readings checked. It is often replaced as a first step for these symptoms.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsation from warped front rotors
issues.sym: The brake pedal and steering wheel pulse or shake when slowing from speed.
issues.why: The front brakes on these cars are sensitive to rotor runout (wobble), so small amounts of uneven wear show up as pulsation. Brakes are the most-reported problem area for the 1998 S90.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replace them with good-quality rotors and make sure the hub faces are clean when they go on.

issues.t: A/C leaks or stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only cools at times.
issues.why: Steel bolts threaded into aluminum lines at the compressor corrode and leak refrigerant, and the compressor clutch can fail.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before recharging. Repairing the leaking fitting is a small job; a failed compressor is much bigger.

issues.t: Rear air suspension compressor fails
issues.sym: A suspension warning on the dash, the rear sitting low, or the self-leveling rear suspension not raising the car.
issues.why: On cars with rear air suspension, the compressor can wear out and blow its fuse. Volvo extended the warranty on this compressor for 2017-2020 S90 and V90 models.
issues.next: Ask a Volvo dealer to check your VIN for the extended coverage before paying. The fix is a new compressor and fuse.

issues.t: 12V battery drains or critical charge warning
issues.sym: A 12V battery or critical charge message, a car that will not start after sitting, or electronics acting up.
issues.why: Volvo has issued many bulletins for 12V battery drain on these cars, including drain while a plug-in hybrid is on its charging cable, modules that stay awake, and false warnings that need a software update.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and the car checked for software updates before buying parts. Bulletins tell dealers not to replace some modules when only a software fix is needed.

issues.t: Center screen freezes, restarts or loses GPS
issues.sym: The center touchscreen goes black, reboots while driving, gets stuck, or shows "Searching for GPS". Audio may be distorted.
issues.why: Software faults in the infotainment unit. Early cars used Volvo Sensus; 2022 and newer use the Google-based system, which has had its own list of bulletins.
issues.next: Make sure all software updates are installed. Dealers can reload the infotainment unit; hardware is rarely needed.

issues.t: Parking brake service message or brake will not release
issues.sym: A "Parking brake service required" message, or the electronic parking brake light stays on. In rare cases early cars would not start after being parked.
issues.why: Software faults in the electronic parking brake system. Volvo released several bulletins and updates for it.
issues.next: Have the brake codes read and the latest software installed. Check the rear brakes too, as worn pads also trigger messages.

issues.t: Brake vibration or shudder when stopping
issues.sym: The steering wheel or pedal vibrates when braking, or the brakes squeal at low speed.
issues.why: Uneven pad deposits and rotor wear. Volvo bulletins address brake shudder with new front pads, and lockable wheel bolts were also found to cause vibration. RepairPal owners report rear rotor vibration as well.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and the pads checked. New pads (and rotors if worn) usually fix it.

issues.t: Harsh shift when putting it in gear
issues.sym: A hard clunk when shifting from Park to Reverse, or from Reverse or Neutral into Drive.
issues.why: A data error in the transmission control module on early cars. Volvo released a software fix.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to update the transmission software.

issues.t: Transmission jumps back into Park after starting
issues.sym: Right after starting, you select Drive or Reverse and the car shifts itself back into Park.
issues.why: A software fault covered by a 2024 Volvo bulletin.
issues.next: Have a dealer install the current software. Make sure the car is actually in gear before taking your foot off the brake.

issues.t: Rear electric motor knocking or bearing noise
issues.sym: A knock, whine or rumble from the rear of the car, mostly when the plug-in hybrid drives on electric power.
issues.why: The T8 has an electric motor driving the rear wheels (ERAD). Volvo has bulletins for bearing noise in it and a repair kit for knocking on long-range models.
issues.next: Have a dealer check it under warranty. Hybrid parts often have longer coverage than the basic warranty.

issues.t: Mild-hybrid starter-generator charging fault
issues.sym: Warning lights or a charging error message, and the engine stop/start may stop working.
issues.why: B5 and B6 versions use a 48-volt starter-generator. Volvo issued bulletins for its generator module and position sensor faults.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes; many cases need software or a module covered by warranty.

issues.t: Check engine light with misfire code
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a misfire or engine computer code, often without any rough running.
issues.why: Volvo bulletins tie several of these codes to software and tell dealers not to replace parts; one needs an oil and filter change.
issues.next: Have codes read and the software brought up to date before replacing coils or plugs.

issues.t: Creaking steering wheel or dead audio buttons
issues.sym: A creak when turning the wheel, or the right-hand steering wheel buttons stop working now and then.
issues.why: Volvo bulletins cover creaking from the steering wheel module, a rubber grommet in the firewall, and faulty right-side switch panels.
issues.next: Mention it at your next service; it is a known fix covered by bulletins.

issues.t: Weak heat or uneven climate airflow
issues.sym: Little air from the vents, the system blowing hot or cold by itself, or slow cabin heating.
issues.why: Several climate control bulletins cover airflow, sudden temperature changes (fixed with software) and heating performance on newer cars.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for climate software updates first.

issues.t: A/C drain can leak water into the cabin (recall)
issues.sym: Water on the front floor, especially after the A/C has been running.
issues.why: The A/C drain hose can let a lot of water into the cabin, where it could reach airbag wiring and affect deployment in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Front passenger seat belt buckle can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: The front passenger buckle can separate from its bracket, so the passenger may not be held properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free repair.

issues.t: Curtain air bag bolts can break (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: Bolts holding the side curtain air bags can break, so the curtain may not deploy correctly.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the bolts for free.

issues.t: Crash location may not reach emergency services (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs, though connected services may misbehave.
issues.why: A connectivity module software error can stop the car from sending its GPS location after a crash.
issues.next: Have the free software fix done at a dealer.

issues.t: Front seat may be missing mounting nuts (recall)
issues.sym: Possible looseness in the front seat, though often nothing is noticed.
issues.why: Nuts could be missing from the front seat structure, which affects seat position and protection in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the seat inspected.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking may not work (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; the automatic braking may simply fail to react to an obstacle.
issues.why: A software and hardware mismatch can stop the automatic emergency braking from detecting obstacles.
issues.next: Have the free software update installed.

issues.t: Fuel pump fuse can blow and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump can blow its fuse and stop working.
issues.next: Have the dealer fit the updated fuse for free.

issues.t: High-voltage battery can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a problem.
issues.why: A fault inside the plug-in hybrid battery can make a module overheat and short circuit, even when parked and switched off.
issues.next: Do not charge the car until the recall repair is done. The dealer inspects the battery, replaces bad modules and adds monitoring software.

issues.t: Airbag control unit may not be secured (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: The airbag control unit may not be fastened to the body and could come loose in a crash.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and tighten it for free.

issues.t: Seat belt may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat may feel loose after installation with the seat belt.
issues.why: The seat belt locking retractor can switch off too early, so it may not hold a child seat tight.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace affected belts.

issues.t: ABS and stability control can shut off (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, stability or traction warning lights.
issues.why: A diagnostic error in brake control software can switch off ABS, stability control and traction control.
issues.next: Install the free over-the-air update or visit a dealer.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays blank or does not show the camera when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: A software fault can stop the rearview camera image from showing. Volvo replaced its first remedy with a second one.
issues.next: Get the free software update, even if the first recall fix was already done.
